chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulaym al-Farra' from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man who makes the vagina of his slave-girl permissible for his brother.
He said: There is no objection to that. I said: But he has impregnated her. He said: Her child is attached to him, and the slave-girl is returned to her master.

key_terms.أَوْلَدَهَا: He impregnated her / She bore his child
key_terms.فَرْجَ: Vagina / Genitals (used here for sexual permission)
key_terms.يُضَمُّ إِلَيْهِ: It is attached to him (referring to lineage/ownership of the child)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave-girl who is married to another man and becomes pregnant in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific legal consequences of *tahlil* (temporary marriage for divorce purposes) involving a slave-girl, establishing that offspring from the second husband belong to him and the girl reverts to her original master. It highlights the distinct Shia juristic view on paternity and ownership rights in this contractual arrangement, distinguishing it from broader Sunni interpretations of *tahlil*. The ruling underscores the practical application of marital contracts within the slave-ownership framework prevalent in early Islamic society.
